# Feature: Open Shadow Roots & Virtualized Lists

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-037
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_interaction_wave2.md`

Close the two capability gaps P12 exposed, so the widget gauntlet's last two patterns pass **because the engine can drive them**, not because a fixture froze a known failure.

Both gaps are structural blindness, verified in the source rather than assumed:

- **Open shadow roots.** Every path that mints an addressable element uses a flat-tree query. `discovery/interactable-scan.ts:48` scans with `document.querySelectorAll(...)`; `browser/agent-controller.ts:387` resolves handles with a _second, independent_ `page.$$(INTERACTABLE_SELECTOR)`; the deterministic replay port at `executor/step-handlers/fill-element.ts:237` uses a third copy of the same `page.$$`; the JSDOM test port uses `document.querySelector`/`querySelectorAll` (`tests/support/widget-test-port.ts:162,169`). None of these cross a shadow boundary — measured: with an open shadow root hosting a `<select>`, `document.querySelectorAll('select').length` is `0`. A control inside an open shadow root is therefore **structurally absent from observation**, gets no ref, and cannot be filled, clicked, or named. `packages/core/src` and `packages/agent/src` contain no shadow-DOM handling at all today (the only `shadow` tokens are CSS variables and one comment at `agent-controller.ts:1218` noting the old hit-test _could not_ see through shadow roots).
- **Virtualized lists.** No widget driver, port, or engine module contains a scroll operation of any kind — `grep -n "scroll" packages/core/src/widgets/**` returns nothing. `option/candidates.ts:collectCandidates` reads `root.querySelectorAll(...)` **once**, so a listbox that mounts only the rows currently in its viewport can offer the engine nothing beyond its first window. The result today is `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE` / `value-not-offered` for a value the widget genuinely has.

After this feature:

- **One traversal mints records and handles together.** The composed-tree scan walks through **open** shadow roots and returns the raw records _and_ the element list from a single in-page pass, so a ref can no longer be bound to a different element than the one it was described from. Today's two independent traversals are held in step only by a doc comment demanding two selector constants stay "byte-identical" (`agent-controller.ts:32-38`) — that comment and one of the constants are deleted, because the coupling they guard is removed rather than documented.
- **Closed shadow roots stay unsupported, deliberately and visibly.** `host.shadowRoot` is `null` for a closed root — the page does not expose it, and no piercing library or DOM tagging is used to get around that (plan §3, §8, §12 item 6). A closed-shadow control is **absent from observation**, which is the correct outcome and is asserted as such. It is not a gauntlet pass.
- **A listbox can be scrolled inside its own container, once, boundedly, and only when it needs to be.** A new counted mutating port action advances the option list's **own** scrollable region — never the window — behind a structural entry condition, deduplicating option identities across mounted windows and stopping the moment a window contributes nothing new.
- **The gallery reaches 17.** Exactly two fixtures: **virtualized listbox** (protocol tier) and **open-shadow-root select** (agent real-browser tier). FEAT-034 may not begin until all 17 pass.

**The hard constraint on every line of this work** (memory → General, plan §1): **no website-specific logic.** Both capabilities are generic structural patterns — a shadow root is a platform feature, a scroll container is `overflow-y: auto`. No host, brand, or site token may appear in any signal, selector, threshold, or log field. Plan §10 is explicit about the one place this is tempting: open-shadow evidence records **only** the structural token `open-shadow`, never a host discriminator. Site names may appear solely in a fixture's leading header comment as provenance.

**Explicitly out of scope**, stated so no one mistakes silence for coverage:

- **Closed shadow roots** — permanently, by design.
- **The serializable element-path codec.** `WidgetContainer.path` and `WidgetCandidate.path` address elements as child-index chains resolved from `document.documentElement`; that idiom is copy-pasted into 15 page-context function bodies across 6 files (Puppeteer serializes only the body, so it cannot be imported). Its `parentElement` walk terminates at a shadow boundary and returns `[]`, so a shadow-hosted **popup container** resolves to "no container" — an honest failure, never a wrong element. Making that codec composed-aware is a separate, larger change; FEAT-037 delivers what plan §5 names — _observation and ref resolution_ — which is handle-addressed and is exactly what the open-shadow **native select** seam of plan §9 needs. Recorded in `.spec-lite/TODO.md`.
- **The combobox driver's candidate collection.** The virtual scan is wired into the `option` family (`listboxDriver`), whose fixture this is. `combobox/combobox-driver.ts` is 692 rung-structured lines that FEAT-034 is about to restructure into declarative rungs; reusing the helper there belongs with that work, not against it. Recorded in `.spec-lite/TODO.md`.
- **No new stable error code.** FEAT-037 adds none. A virtualized list that genuinely does not offer the value still returns `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE` / `value-not-offered`, now carrying deduplicated cross-window evidence.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does **not** exist, and plan §4 states plainly that **no new relational schema and no Data Modeller pass is needed for this plan**. There are therefore **no tables, no columns, no migrations, no indexes, and no foreign keys in this feature** — inventing any would be fiction. The shapes below are **TypeScript contract shapes**: in-memory values passed across the widget port and the observation seam, plus bounded evidence recorded in the attempt ledger. They are designed here because plan §4 gives only the conceptual `OpenShadowTarget` / `VirtualListCursor` concepts.

### Entities & Attributes

**`OpenShadowTarget`** — an addressable element exposed through an **open** composed tree. It is not a new runtime object: it is the set of guarantees the existing `RawInteractable` → ref → `ElementHandle` chain must now satisfy for an element whose root node is a `ShadowRoot`. Modelling it as a parallel type would create a second kind of ref, which is precisely the drift the one-traversal invariant exists to prevent.

- `elementIndex` (`number`) — position in the **single** element array returned by the traversal that produced this record. NOT NULL. Replaces `RawInteractable.selectorIndex`, which indexed a _different_ query's NodeList. The rename is the point: nothing may index a list this record did not come from.
- `composedScope` (`'document' | 'open-shadow'`) — whether the element's root node is the document or an open `ShadowRoot`. NOT NULL. **Internal.** Never projected into `AgentInteractable`, never serialized to the model, never written to `tool-calls.jsonl` — asserted by test, because `browser-common.ts:305` passes `observation.interactables` to the model wholesale and any field added there becomes model-visible payload that FEAT-032's frozen goldens would flag.
- `rootNodeDepth` (`number`) — how many open shadow boundaries were crossed to reach the element (0 for light DOM). Internal; bounds the traversal and makes the recursion cap assertable.
- The element's `role`, `name`, `group`, `scope`, `value`, `visible`, … keep today's meanings and today's types. Three of their **computations** change, because each currently reaches for `document` and must reach for the element's own root:
  - `name` via `aria-labelledby` → resolve ids against `element.getRootNode()`, not `document` (ids are scoped per shadow root).
  - `name` via `label[for=…]` → same.
  - `group` / `scope` → walk the **composed** ancestor chain: `node.parentElement ?? (node.getRootNode() as ShadowRoot).host`.

**`ScrollFrame`** — what one bounded container-scroll step observed. Returned by the new port action; `null` when the container owns no scrollable region.

- `scrollTop` (`number`) — the region's scroll offset after the step.
- `scrollHeight` (`number`), `clientHeight` (`number`) — the range. **Evidence, not a stop condition** (see the constraint below).
- `moved` (`boolean`) — `scrollTop` differs from its value before this step.
- `atEnd` (`boolean`) — `scrollTop + clientHeight >= scrollHeight - 1`.

**`VirtualListCursor`** — bounded progress evidence for a scrollable option container, accumulated across mounted windows. Plan §4's concept, made concrete.

- `windows` (`number`) — mounted windows examined; always ≥ 1 (the initial window costs no scroll).
- `scrolls` (`number`) — scroll actions charged. Also charged against `WidgetBudget.maxActions`.
- `seen` (`ReadonlySet<string>` → serialized as a capped array) — deduplicated **content-derived** option identities: `normalizeText(name) + '\u0000' + role`. Content-derived is required, not stylistic: a virtual list recycles DOM nodes, so a node- or path-derived identity reports the same recycled `<li>` as a new option forever and no-progress can never be detected. Bounded by `MAX_TRACKED_OPTION_IDENTITIES` (500).
- `offered` (`readonly string[]`) — display labels in first-seen order, capped at `MAX_RANKED_OFFERED` (10, already exported from `interaction/query-plan.ts:186`). This is the only part of the cursor that reaches a model-visible payload; it is page text and passes the same sanitizer as every other observed label.
- `scrollTop` / `scrollHeight` / `clientHeight` / `atEnd` (`number` / `boolean`) — the last `ScrollFrame`.
- `stoppedBecause` (`VirtualListStop`) — NOT NULL. The no-progress reason plan §10 requires in the ledger.

**`VirtualListStop`** — a closed discriminated set. Every exit is named; there is no "just finished" arm, because an unnamed exit is an unbounded loop waiting to happen.

`'matched'` | `'not-scrollable'` | `'reached-end'` | `'no-new-options'` | `'scroll-position-unchanged'` | `'step-cap'` | `'budget'`

**`WidgetBudget.maxScrollSteps`** (`number`, default 8) — the **declared** action cap plan §5 requires, sitting beside the existing `maxPagingSteps` in `defaultWidgetBudget` (`widgets/types.ts`). Declared per budget rather than hardcoded in the driver, so a caller can lower it and a test can pin it.

### Relationships

- One traversal produces one `RawInteractable[]` **and** one `Element[]` of the same length ordering, related by `elementIndex` — a 1:1 correspondence that is structural (same array, same pass) rather than maintained by convention. This is the feature's central correctness property.
- One `WidgetTarget` (a ref) 1:1 one live `ElementHandle` held in `AgentBrowserController.refs`. Unchanged, except that the handle may now live inside an open shadow tree; `isConnected` is `true` for such a node (verified), so the existing staleness contract needs no change.
- One `listboxDriver.drive()` invocation produces at most one `VirtualListCursor`; the cursor produces exactly one `AttemptRecord` in the ledger when any scroll was charged, and none when the entry condition did not fire.
- `VirtualListCursor.offered` N:1 `MAX_RANKED_OFFERED` — the same cap already governing every other offered set, reused rather than re-chosen.

### Indexes & Constraints

- **No tables, no indexes, no migrations.** Filesystem/run-artifact storage is unchanged; no run directory is rewritten.
- **Single-traversal invariant** — after this feature, `packages/core/src/browser/agent-controller.ts` contains **no** interactable query of its own. `INTERACTABLE_SELECTOR` and the "must stay byte-identical" doc comment (`:32-38`) are deleted, and a source-boundary test asserts neither the controller nor the executor's replay port pairs a separately-queried handle list with an index minted elsewhere.
- **No DOM mutation in the scan** (plan §8, memory → Architecture "detection never mutates page state"): the composed traversal sets no attribute, injects no marker, and adds no node. Asserted by a test that snapshots the page's full composed markup before and after an observation and compares byte-for-byte. `option/candidates.ts:withTag` is a pre-existing **action-stage** tagging fallback inside `clickCandidate` and is explicitly out of this rule's scope — but it is equally explicitly **not** an acceptable way to align handles.
- **Closed roots are unrepresentable, not filtered.** The traversal descends only into `element.shadowRoot`, which the platform returns as `null` for a closed root. There is no closed-root branch to get wrong.
- **Scroll targets the container's own region only.** The scrollable region is the nearest element, searched from the container's own subtree outward to the container itself, whose computed **`overflowY`** is `auto` or `scroll`; when several qualify, prefer one with `scrollHeight > clientHeight`. `document.scrollingElement`, `document.body`, `document.documentElement`, and `window` are excluded by construction. Reading `overflowY` (not the `overflow` shorthand) is required: the shorthand computes to `""` where the page set only the longhand (verified in JSDOM).
- **Layout metrics are evidence, never the sole stop condition.** `scrollHeight`/`clientHeight` are `0` in any environment without a layout engine (verified: JSDOM reports `0`/`0` for a styled overflow container), so `atEnd` computed from them is vacuously true there. Termination is identity-first: `no-new-options` and `scroll-position-unchanged` are the load-bearing rules; `atEnd` and `reached-end` are corroborating evidence. A driver that stops only on `atEnd` would terminate instantly under JSDOM and loop to the cap in Chrome — both wrong.
- **Bounded everything.** `MAX_TRACKED_OPTION_IDENTITIES` = 500 identities; `maxScrollSteps` = 8; `MAX_RESOLUTION_INTERACTABLES` = 400 (existing) now enforced **inside** the page traversal so a pathological composed tree cannot explode the element array before any handle is minted; shadow recursion depth capped at 16, matching the existing `nameFromContent` depth guard.

### TASK-001: One composed-tree traversal that sees through open shadow roots

- [ ] **Implementation**: Rework `packages/core/src/discovery/interactable-scan.ts` so `scanInteractablesInPage(options: { withElements?: boolean; max?: number } = {})` returns `{ records: RawInteractable[]; elements: Element[] }` from **one** pass. Replace the single `document.querySelectorAll(...)` (`:48`) with an explicit iterative walk that starts at `document.documentElement`, tests each element against the existing role/kind rules, and — when `element.shadowRoot` is non-null — descends into that root's children. Open roots only: the platform returns `null` for a closed root, so there is no closed-root branch to write and none to get wrong. Do not descend into `<slot>` assigned nodes (slotted content lives in the light DOM and is already visited); dedupe by node identity so a slotted element is never recorded twice. Bound the walk with `max` (the controller passes `MAX_RESOLUTION_INTERACTABLES`) and a shadow-depth cap of 16, matching the existing `nameFromContent` guard. Record `elementIndex` (index into the returned `elements`), `composedScope: 'document' | 'open-shadow'`, and `rootNodeDepth`; delete `selectorIndex`. Fix the three `document`-anchored computations so they use the element's own root: `aria-labelledby` id lookup and `label[for=…]` resolve against `element.getRootNode()`; `computeGroup` and `computeScope` walk the composed ancestor chain (`node.parentElement ?? (node.getRootNode() as ShadowRoot).host`). `withElements: false` returns `elements: []` so the discovery path at `observe.ts:120` can keep its by-value `page.evaluate` (a DOM node in a by-value return is not serializable). The function body stays fully self-contained — Puppeteer serializes only the body, which is why there is one function with a flag rather than two functions sharing a helper. **The scan sets no attribute, injects no marker, and adds no node.** Update `observe.ts:buildAgentPageSnapshot` to accept pre-scanned records, and update `tests/discovery/interactable-scan.spec.ts` call sites to read `.records`.

A shadow-hosted control named by an `aria-labelledby` id that exists **only inside its own shadow root** is named correctly, while a same-valued id in the document does not leak into it — the assertion that proves root-scoped resolution rather than `document.getElementById`. A shadow-hosted control inside a `role="dialog"` **host** reports `scope: 'dialog'` and the host's `group`, proving composed ancestry. `records.length === elements.length` and every `record.elementIndex` indexes its own element. `composedScope` is `'open-shadow'` for shadow content and `'document'` for light DOM. Nested open shadow roots (depth 2) are reached; depth beyond 16 is not. `max` truncates both arrays together. A page whose full composed markup is captured before and after a scan is **byte-identical** afterwards — the no-mutation assertion. Slotted light-DOM content is recorded exactly once.

### TASK-004: A counted, container-only scroll action on every widget port

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add to `packages/core/src/widgets/types.ts`: `ScrollFrame` (§2), `WidgetBudget.maxScrollSteps` (default `8` in `defaultWidgetBudget`), and `WidgetPort.scrollContainer(container: WidgetContainer, step?: number): Promise<ScrollFrame | null>`. It is a **port method, not a free function over `port.evaluate`**, precisely so FEAT-032's `PORT_ACTION_KIND` counts it as a **mutation**; classify it there. Semantics: resolve the container by its existing child-index path; find the scrollable region as the nearest element searched from the container's own subtree outward to the container itself whose computed **`overflowY`** is `auto` or `scroll` (read the longhand — the `overflow` shorthand computes to `""` when only the longhand was set, verified), preferring one with `scrollHeight > clientHeight` when several qualify; return `null` when none exists. Never touch `window`, `document.scrollingElement`, `document.body`, or `document.documentElement` — excluded explicitly, because "scroll only the owning container" is plan §5's rule and scrolling the window would move the whole page under an agent that did not ask for it. Advance by `step ?? Math.max(1, clientHeight - overlap)` rows-worth using `scrollTop` assignment (not a wheel event: a wheel dispatch targets whatever is under the cursor and can reach the window), then dispatch a `scroll` event on the region so a renderer keyed to the event re-mounts promptly — a renderer keyed to `scrollTop` is idempotent under the extra event Chrome also fires. Return the resulting `ScrollFrame` including `moved`. Implement on all **three** ports: `AgentBrowserController`, the executor's replay port, and `WidgetTestPort`. Note for the JSDOM port: `scrollTop` is settable and retains its value, but `scrollHeight`/`clientHeight` are always `0` (verified), which is exactly why §2 makes layout metrics evidence rather than a stop condition — the test port needs no geometry simulation, and the fixture drives its own re-mount from the `scroll` event and `scrollTop`. **This is an action, never a probe:** `scrollContainer` may only be called from `drive()`, never from `detect()` or `detectOpen()` (memory → Architecture: detection never mutates page state). Enforce it with a test.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: A container whose region declares `overflow-y: auto` returns a `ScrollFrame`; one with no such region returns `null`. The region chosen is inside the container, never `document.scrollingElement` — asserted by scrolling a page that is _also_ window-scrollable and checking `window.scrollY` is unchanged. Assigning past the end clamps and reports `moved: false` on the following step. A `scroll` event fires on the region. `PORT_ACTION_KIND` classifies `scrollContainer` as `'mutation'`, and removing that entry fails typecheck (the guarantee FEAT-032 TASK-001 built this table for). A driver calling `scrollContainer` from `detect()` fails an explicit detection-purity test. All three port implementations satisfy one shared conformance test.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the widget port contract (bounded container scrolling and its mutation accounting).
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test -- widget-port widget-regressions` passes; deleting `scrollContainer` from `PORT_ACTION_KIND` fails `pnpm --filter @yantra/core typecheck`; the window-scroll guard test fails if the implementation falls back to `document.scrollingElement`.

### TASK-005: Bounded, deduplicated virtual-list scanning in the listbox driver

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `packages/core/src/widgets/option/virtual-list.ts` exporting `VirtualListCursor`, `VirtualListStop`, `MAX_TRACKED_OPTION_IDENTITIES` (500), `optionIdentity(candidate)` (`normalizeText(name) + '\u0000' + role` — content-derived, because a virtual list recycles DOM nodes and a node/path-derived identity can never detect no-progress), and `scanVirtualOptions(port, container, requested, budget)`. The loop: collect the current window with the existing `collectCandidates`, rank it with `rankCandidate`, and **return immediately on a match or an ambiguity** so the candidate is always clicked from the window it was found in — never from a stale snapshot a later scroll has recycled. Otherwise fold the window's identities into `seen`, append unseen labels to `offered` (capped at `MAX_RANKED_OFFERED`), call `port.scrollContainer`, wait for the re-render with the existing `readWhenStable` (`interaction/settle.ts`) rather than a fixed sleep, and repeat. Terminate on: `matched`; `not-scrollable` (`scrollContainer` returned `null`); `no-new-options` (the window contributed zero unseen identities); `scroll-position-unchanged` (`moved: false`); `step-cap` (`budget.maxScrollSteps`); `budget` (`budget.deadlineMs` or `maxActions`); `reached-end` is corroborating evidence recorded alongside, never the sole stop. Wire it into `listboxDriver.drive` **behind a structural entry condition**: only after `rankCandidate` on the initial window returns `kind: 'none'`. Memory (2026-08-30) requires diagnostic work be paid for only on the path that needs it and that it be asserted by counting the operation — so a listbox whose target is in the first window must charge **zero** scrolls. Charge each scroll against `actions`. On failure, keep the existing `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE` / `value-not-offered` code and cause (no new code) and carry the cursor's deduplicated `offered`; the hint must keep naming an engineered move the caller can actually make (re-issue one of the offered labels) and must **not** advise scrolling, which the agent has no tool for (memory → Coding Standards). Record one `AttemptRecord` when any scroll was charged: `strategy: 'scroll-container'`, `axis: 'what'` (the rung varies what the widget has been given a chance to offer; it changes neither the target node nor the typing mechanics), `detail` carrying **only** the bounded scroll count and the `stoppedBecause` token — plan §10's "bounded scroll count and no-progress reason", with no page text and no host token.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: A target in the initial mounted window commits with **zero** `scrollContainer` calls — the entry-condition assertion, counted. A target three windows down is reached, committed, and the ledger records the exact scroll count and `stoppedBecause: 'matched'`. A list that mounts the **same** rows on every scroll stops with `no-new-options` after exactly one unproductive window, not at the step cap. A container that will not move stops with `scroll-position-unchanged`. A genuinely long list of unique rows that never contains the value stops at `step-cap` with `scrolls === maxScrollSteps`. `offered` is deduplicated across windows, in first-seen order, and never exceeds `MAX_RANKED_OFFERED`; `seen` never exceeds `MAX_TRACKED_OPTION_IDENTITIES`. A list that recycles DOM nodes (same nodes, new text) still detects progress and still detects its absence — the assertion that proves identity is content-derived. Budget exhaustion mid-scan returns `budget` and does not exceed `maxActions`. The failure's `details.hint` names re-issuing an offered label and contains no instruction to scroll; the emitted failure JSON contains no `cause` key (Wave 1 invariant preserved).
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for the option widget family (virtualized-list scanning, its bounds, and its ledger evidence).
- **Verify**: `pnpm --filter @yantra/core test -- virtual-list` passes; temporarily removing the `kind: 'none'` entry condition makes the zero-scroll first-window test red, proving the scan is not on the hot path.
- **Depends on**: TASK-004

Choose a target row far enough down that at least two scrolls are required, so the count is meaningful. The closed-shadow control is asserted **absent from the observation** as an extra assertion in the case body — deliberately **not** a third `ExpectedOutcome` arm: FEAT-032 made "we cannot do this yet" unrepresentable on purpose, and a closed root is not a pass (plan §12 item 6). The closed-shadow control's name appears **nowhere** in the observation payload. ## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A. No credentials, keychain access, consent surface, or secret fill is touched. The agent-tier fixture deliberately drives a non-secret control; secret-fill coverage already lives in `e2e/agent-browser.spec.ts` and duplicating it here would widen a test fixture's blast radius for no new signal.
- **Error Handling**: **No new stable error code and no change to an existing one** — the frozen code-set snapshot FEAT-032 TASK-007 introduced must remain unchanged by this feature, and that is a verification, not an aspiration. A virtualized list that does not offer the value keeps `WIDGET_TARGET_UNREACHABLE` / `value-not-offered`, now with cross-window `offered` evidence. A closed-shadow control produces no error at all: it is absent, and the caller's failure is whatever it already was for a control that is not on the page. `cause` stays internal and is never serialized. `scrollContainer` returning `null` is a normal, named outcome (`not-scrollable`), never an exception.
- **Logging**: Structured Pino only; no new sink and no new artifact. The controller's observation log gains a fixed-token open-shadow **count**; the attempt ledger gains one `scroll-container` record carrying only a bounded count and a `VirtualListStop` token. Plan §10 is satisfied by construction rather than by review: both fields are literals or integers, so no host, brand, or page text can reach them. `offered` labels are page text and pass the same sanitizer as every other observed label.
- **Security**: No network access beyond the existing loopback fixture host; both fixtures are local static files. No page mutation from any detection or observation path — the composed scan tags nothing, which is the "detection never mutates page state" rule (memory → Architecture) applied to the one place plan §8 names as tempting. Scrolling is a mutation and is confined to `drive()`, bounded by a declared cap, and confined to the widget's own container so it can never move the page under the user. Closed shadow roots are not merely unpierced but unreachable — the platform withholds them, and no workaround is introduced.
- **No website-specific logic** (memory → General, plan §1): every signal here is a platform or style primitive — `element.shadowRoot`, `getRootNode()`, computed `overflowY`, `scrollTop`. There is no selector table, no host branch, and no tuned constant keyed to any site. Site tokens may appear only in a fixture's leading header comment, mechanically enforced by FEAT-032's provenance-containment census.
- **Two independent contracts, checked explicitly** (memory, 2026-08-31): `AgentBrowserController` and the executor's replay `WidgetPort` are separate implementations of "what is addressable on this page". TASK-003 exists because a guarantee added to one does not reach the other, and because agent-time and replay-time capability diverging is how a promoted workflow silently stops working. They share the traversal and keep their own projections — deliberately not unified.
- **Diagnostic cost** (memory, 2026-08-30): the virtual scan runs only behind a structural entry condition and is asserted by **counting** the operation, because a silent extra page read is invisible in every other signal. The composed traversal replaces two page round-trips (`evaluate` + `$$`) with one, so observation gets cheaper rather than more expensive; the pinned `expectedReads` on the retrofitted fixtures is what will say so.
- **Testing/architecture**: `packages/core` must never import `@yantra/agent` (memory → Project Structure) — respected: the agent-tier fixture lives in the `e2e` workspace package, which is where real Chrome plus wrapped tools already runs. Tests stay in mirrored `tests/` directories. Both new suites carry `@no-llm` so they run under `pnpm test:no-llm` on macOS, Windows, and Ubuntu. Any assertion that reads a persisted artifact or fixture file goes through FEAT-032's `readUtf8` — a bare Windows PowerShell 5.1 read has produced two false mojibake alarms (2026-07-12, 2026-08-29).
